body_markdown:
According to the CDC, more than 1 in 5 U.S. teens now has obesity, and the number keeps rising. Obesity is more than a number on a scale. It raises a teen's risk of type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, fatty liver disease, sleep apnea, and joint problems. It can also weigh on mental health. It can add to anxiety, depression, and low self-esteem at an already hard age.


Have you tried diet and lifestyle changes that did not last? A GLP-1 telehealth program for teens may be a safe next step. GLP-1 medicines are a type of medicine that helps manage weight.[Blueberry Balance makes it possible for your teen to get FDA-approved GLP-1 treatment online.](https://balance.blueberrypediatrics.com/)[Board-certified pediatricians](https://www.blueberrypediatrics.com/our-pediatricians) (doctors with special training in kids' health) lead the whole program, and your teen never has to leave home.


Why think about GLP-1 medicine for a teen? Sometimes severe obesity does not improve, even after real effort with food, exercise, and new habits. When that happens, health risks can add up fast during the teen years. These include type 2 diabetes and heart disease. That is why the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), the main group of U.S. children's doctors, now recommends that medicine be considered as part of a full treatment plan for teens with obesity.


Blueberry Balance is a 100% virtual weight care program built just for teens ages 12 and older. Here is how it works, who can join, and what to expect.


## What Is Blueberry Balance?


Blueberry Balance is a telehealth program led by pediatricians. Your teen can get GLP-1 medicine online, with a doctor guiding each step. Most weight loss clinics are built for adults. This one is built for teens. It fits their body, their growth, and how they feel.


The program uses only FDA-approved, brand-name GLP-1 medicines. It does not use compounded GLP-1s (versions mixed by a pharmacy that the FDA has not approved). Wegovy (semaglutide) is the only GLP-1 medicine the FDA has approved for weight management in teens ages 12 and older. Your teen's pediatrician picks the best plan for them, based on their needs and current FDA approvals.


The medicine is just one part. Your teen also gets ongoing behavior support, food guidance, and exercise coaching, plus continuous medical monitoring. This matches the AAP 2023 guideline. That guideline recommends medicine as an addition to intensive treatment, not a replacement for it. That treatment changes health habits and lifestyle: structured, family-based support around food, activity, and behavior, delivered over many hours of contact.


## How It Works


Getting started is simple. The whole process is virtual, so your teen never misses school for a visit.


### Step 1: Meet Online


Your teen starts with a full video visit with a board-certified pediatrician. The care team looks at your teen's health history, current BMI (body mass index, a number based on height and weight, compared with other teens the same age and sex), and overall health. They also run a few required checks. These include screens for eating disorders, depression, and metabolic health (things like blood sugar). These checks help make sure GLP-1 medicine is safe and clinically appropriate for your teen.


### Step 2: Get a Plan Made for Your Teen


If your teen qualifies, the pediatrician builds a plan just for them. It includes the right medicine at the right dose. It also adds food coaching and behavior support. These medicines need to be started slowly. The dose goes up little by little, and the timeline depends on the medicine. So the plan includes frequent video check-ins. These help the team track progress and handle any side effects.


### Step 3: Ongoing Monitoring and Support


Managing weight takes time, and Blueberry Balance stays with your teen for the long run. Your teen gets regular video visits, lab result reviews, growth checks, and mental health check-ins. Tools like smart scales let the care team follow progress between visits, all from home.

## Who Is Eligible for GLP-1 Treatment?


Wegovy is FDA-approved for teens ages 12 and older whose BMI is at or above the 95th percentile for their age and sex. That threshold is the medical definition of obesity in this age group. Still, the right choice is different for every teen. Your teen's pediatrician will look at their health, their history, and their needs to decide if GLP-1 treatment is clinically appropriate for them.


Some health conditions can keep your teen from using GLP-1 medicine. Your teen may not be able to take it if they, or a family member, have had a rare thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). The same is true for a rare inherited condition called Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN2).


GLP-1 medicines also carry FDA warnings. These include:


- sudden swelling of the pancreas (acute pancreatitis)
- gallbladder problems (acute gallbladder disease)
- low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), especially when taken with certain diabetes medicines that raise insulin (called insulin secretagogues)
- thoughts of suicide or self-harm (suicidal ideation or behavior)


Your teen's pediatrician goes over all of the eligibility rules and safety issues at the first visit. The team also monitors for these risks all through treatment.


## What to Expect: Common Side Effects


GLP-1 medicines are usually well tolerated, but stomach and gut side effects are common, mostly while the dose is going up. In the STEP TEENS clinical trial, about 62% of teens taking semaglutide reported these side effects. About 42% of teens taking a placebo (a dummy treatment with no medicine) reported them too. The most common side effects are:


- nausea
- vomiting
- diarrhea
- belly pain
- constipation


These are usually mild to moderate. They often get better as your teen's body gets used to the medicine. The Blueberry Balance care team monitors for side effects at every visit. They adjust the plan as needed to keep your teen comfortable.


## Our Pediatric Team

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can my teen get GLP-1 medicine through telehealth?


Yes. GLP-1 medicines like semaglutide (Wegovy) are not controlled substances. So they are not held back by the federal telehealth rules that limit some other medicines. Blueberry Balance pediatricians do a careful video exam first. They prescribe FDA-approved medicine when it is clinically appropriate. Wegovy is approved for weight management in teens ages 12 and older.


### How does online prescribing work?


Your teen meets a board-certified pediatrician over secure video. The doctor reviews their health history and runs the required checks. If your teen qualifies, the doctor prescribes the right GLP-1 medicine. The prescription goes to your pharmacy. The care team then follows up often to track progress, adjust the dose, and handle side effects.


### Does telehealth work as well as in-person care?


Telehealth fits GLP-1 care well. This treatment needs close monitoring, mostly while the dose goes up. Video visits make those check-ins easy to fit in, without missing school. Your teen gets lab work done nearby, and the team reviews the results online. Early research points to telehealth as a promising way to manage medicine and mental health support over time.

We are adding new states over time. Contact us to find out if the program is open in your state.
